summary: Baileys fork @yudzxml/baileys 7.4.1 — static co-occurrence of child_process/http/os in messages-media utility requires human review
details: @yudzxml/baileys is a third-party fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web API library. Static pattern rules matched on lib/Utils/messages-media.js due to co-occurrence of require('child_process'), require('http')/require('https'), require('os'), and POST/fetch calls, alongside the legitimate WhatsApp media host https://mmg.whatsapp.net. These primitives are expected in a WhatsApp media handling module (uploading/downloading media, invoking ffmpeg via child_process for media transcoding, platform detection via os), and the only explicitly cited destination is WhatsApp's own media endpoint. However, this is a fork of a package family with a known history of covert modifications (e.g., silent auto-subscribe/auto-follow inserted into forks), and no traced-code corroboration was available to confirm the child_process usage is limited to media transcoding and that no additional non-first-party destination is contacted. Route to human review to verify the child_process invocations target ffmpeg/media tooling only, that outbound network is confined to WhatsApp infrastructure, and that no covert side-effects using the installer's WhatsApp session identity are wired into exported APIs.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
